title: Investigating the asymmetric chemistry in the disk around the young star HD 142527
question: What is the role of the asymmetric dust trap in setting the chemical composition of the HD 142527 disk, and how does it compare to IRS 48?

what.value: Line properties (frequency, upper level energy, Einstein A coefficient, upper state degeneracy) and partition functions Q(T_rot)

evidence.quote: The line properties (frequency, upper level energy, Einstein $A$ coefficient and upper state degeneracy) have been acquired from *CDMS*.

$Q\left(T_\textnormal{rot}\right)$ is the partition function at $T_\textnormal{rot}$ which, through interpolation, has been obtained from the *Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy* (*CDMS*; (cite: CDMS01; CDMS05)).

recipe.goal: Search for weak line emission via spectral stacking
recipe.method: Align and stack spectra from different sides of the disk accounting for Keplerian rotation in radial bins from 0.0" to 3.0" (width = 2x beam minor axis, step = 1x beam minor axis)
key_parameters: Radial range 0.0" to 3.0", bin width = 2x minor axis of beam, step = 1x minor axis of beam
assumptions: Keplerian rotation of the disk (d = 157 pc, M_star = 1.69 M_sun, incl = 27 deg, PA = 160 deg)

recipe.goal: Extract disk-integrated line fluxes and 3-sigma upper limits
recipe.method: Extract integrated fluxes using SPECFLUX task with circular apertures (CO isotopologues except 13C18O) or Keplerian masks (all other detections); compute 3-sigma upper limits in a 3.0" circular aperture for non-detections
key_parameters: Circular aperture radius 2.5" to 3.0" for bright CO isotopologues; 3.0" circular aperture for upper limits; channel width delta_v = 0.5 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Calculate disk-averaged column densities and rotational diagram for H2CO
recipe.method: Compute upper level column density N_u^thin from integrated flux, apply optical depth correction C_tau, and convert to N_tot via Boltzmann equation using CDMS partition functions; for H2CO, fit 4 transitions simultaneously with MCMC rotational diagram analysis
key_parameters: T_rot = 35 K for single-transition disk-averaged column densities; Omega = 4.7e-11 sr (annulus ~115 au to ~395 au) for H2CO rotational diagram
assumptions: LTE / Boltzmann level populations; T_rot = 35 K for single transitions

recipe.goal: Extract azimuthally averaged deprojected radial profiles
recipe.method: Deproject and azimuthally average emission using GoFish with radial bin sizes of half the beam minor axis
key_parameters: Bin size = 0.5 x beam minor axis

recipe.goal: Derive mm-sized dust mass from Band 6 continuum
recipe.method: Measure Band 6 continuum flux at 277.51 GHz in a 1.625" circular aperture, compute peak continuum brightness temperature via inverse Planck function, and calculate optically thin dust mass
key_parameters: Aperture radius = 1.625", nu = 277.51 GHz, T_dust = 28.2 K, kappa_nu = 2.8 cm^2 g^-1
assumptions: Optically thin continuum emission; d = 157 pc; kappa_nu = 10 (nu / 1000 GHz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 with beta = 1; T_dust = 28.2 K

recipe.goal: Derive total gas mass and gas-to-dust ratio
recipe.method: Taper 13C18O J=3-2 to C18O J=3-2 beam, extract GoFish radial profiles to ~415 au, convert to 12CO column densities using isotopologue ratios, combine 13C18O in the ring with C18O at r <= 50 au and r >= 350 au, convert to H2 and integrate radial surface density
key_parameters: Radial extent out to ~415 au; C18O used at <=50 au and >=350 au
assumptions: Optically thin emission; 12C/13C = 68 +/- 15; 16O/18O = 557 +/- 30; H2/12CO = 10^4; mean molecular weight = 2.4

recipe.goal: Model 3D dust temperature structure and locate the CO snowline
recipe.method: Construct a 3D radiative transfer model in RADMC-3D with DIANA opacities (via OpTool), visually fitting the dereddened SED and ALMA continuum radial profile to map the 20 K midplane CO snowline
key_parameters: Small grains 0.005-1 um, large grains 0.005-1000 um; R_sub = 0.22 au, R_c,ID = 40 au, gamma = 1; cavity 40-100 au; inner disk h_c = 0.2, psi = 0.05, 50% large grains; outer disk h_c = 0.35, R_c = 150 au, psi = 0.2, 85% large grains; settling chi = 0.1; M_dust = 7.5e-3 M_sun
assumptions: DIANA dust opacities; dust sublimation temperature = 1500 K; A_V = 0.3 mag; L = 9.9 L_sun

score_reason: All 7 ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the software stack (CASA 6.5.1, GoFish, emcee, RADMC-3D, OpTool) is open and clearly identified, and most equations, line parameters, and physical assumptions are explicitly given in the text and tables. However, low-level imaging/self-calibration settings (solint, cell size, multiscale scales, exact Keplerian mask parameters) and a few RADMC-3D outer-disk Gaussian parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets are publicly available archival observations, the analysis relies on standard open-source tools (CASA, GoFish, emcee), and the paper provides clear quantitative answer keys (integrated fluxes, column densities, H2CO rotational temperature, dust mass, and gas mass).
